payload.title: [native-android-3] Sign-out clears session but leaves cached objects/streams in plaintext SQLite — data remanenc...
payload.description:
AUDIT FINDING native-android-3 (medium/isolation, confidence=high, verify-votes +2/-0)

FILE: apps/android/frick/src/main/java/dev/frick/client/FrickClient.kt
LINES: 1000-1003, 665-673

WHAT: FrickClient.signOut() (1000-1003) calls storage.clearPendingAppends() + storage.clearSession() but NOT storage.clearCache(). clearCache() (665-673) is the only thing that wipes local_objects / local_stream_events / frick_cache_metadata, and it is invoked solely from resetCache() (918-920), which neither signOut() nor the demo logout() (FoundationViewModel.kt:395-413) call. Consequently every synced record and stream event the signed-out user pulled — including records shared with them by other users (FrickSharingService) — survives sign-out as plaintext rows on disk. On a shared device where user B signs in next, verifyCacheCompatibility() only throws SESSION_SCOPE_MISMATCH if cache metadata carried a userId (FrickCacheCompatibility.reason, 371-377), but the stale rows physically remain on disk until that check fires, and combined with finding native-android-1 they are unencrypted the whole time.

IMPACT: Personal/shared data from a prior account persists in cleartext after logout, recoverable by the next device user or by anyone with file access — a privacy and tenant-isolation gap, especially on shared/kiosk devices.

SUGGESTED FIX: Have signOut() also call storage.clearCache() (or expose a wipeAll() that clears session + pending + cache + metadata), and call it from the demo logout(). At minimum document that callers must invoke resetCache() on sign-out.
